title: Working with Forms: Beyond v-model
description: Handle form submission, reset, and advanced input events.

slides.title: Form Events: submit, reset
slides.content:
# Handling Form Events

While `v-model` handles two‑way binding, you often need to react to the form's submission or reset actions.

- `@submit` – triggered when the form is submitted (user hits Enter inside a field or clicks submit button).
- `@reset` – triggered when the form is reset (by a `<button type="reset">`).

Always use `.prevent` with `@submit` to avoid page reloads.

slides.title: Input Events: change, input, blur
slides.content:
Beyond `v-model`, you might want to react to specific input events:

- `@input` – triggered on every keystroke (like `v-model` without modifiers).
- `@change` – triggered when the element loses focus after a value change.
- `@blur` – triggered when the element loses focus.

These give you fine‑grained control over user interaction.

quizData.question: Why should you use `.prevent` on form `@submit`?

options.text: To prevent the browser from reloading the page
To submit the form only once

quizData.explanation: `.prevent` calls `event.preventDefault()`, which stops the browser from reloading the page on form submission.
